interactions.title: Check yourself: Linux on the server

questions.prompt: Which command shows which process is listening on port 8080?
questions.explanation: `ss -ltnp` lists listening TCP sockets with numeric ports and the owning process. `ps` knows nothing about ports, and `ping` has no ports at all.

questions.prompt: Which file mode fits a `.env` file containing the database password?
questions.explanation: `600` lets only the owner read and write it. `644` is readable by every user on the server.

questions.prompt: `free -h` shows `free 120Mi` and `available 820Mi` on a 2 GB server. What is true?
options: The server is out of memory
About 820 MiB can still be used by new programs; Linux uses spare memory as cache
The JVM has a memory leak
questions.explanation: Linux fills spare RAM with page cache and releases it on demand. The `available` column is the one that matters.

questions.prompt: ufw allows only 22, 80 and 443, yet a container started with `-p 8080:8080` is reachable from the internet on 8080. Why?
options: Docker's own iptables rules for published ports bypass ufw's rules
questions.explanation: Docker programs iptables for published ports before ufw's rules apply. Publish internal ports on `127.0.0.1` only.

interactions.title: Predict the command: CMD, ENTRYPOINT and friends

questions.prompt: Which command runs for `docker run img --server.port=9090`?

code.source:
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
COPY app.jar /app/app.jar
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app/app.jar"]
CMD ["--server.port=8080"]

questions.explanation: Arguments after the image name replace `CMD`; the `ENTRYPOINT` stays and receives them.

questions.prompt: Which command runs for `docker run img`?
options: The build fails: two CMD lines
questions.explanation: Only the last `CMD` in a Dockerfile takes effect.

questions.prompt: The image ends with `ENTRYPOINT java -jar app.jar`. What happens on `docker stop`?
options: Java receives SIGTERM and shuts down gracefully
`/bin/sh` is PID 1 and does not forward SIGTERM, so Docker kills Java after 10 seconds
questions.explanation: The shell form wraps the command in `/bin/sh -c`. Use the exec form `["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]`.

questions.prompt: The Dockerfile contains `EXPOSE 8080`. You run `docker run -d img` (no `-p`). Can `curl localhost:8080` on the host reach the app?
options: No — EXPOSE only documents the port; nothing is published without -p
Only if the app is a Spring Boot app
questions.explanation: Publishing needs `-p HOST:CONTAINER` (or `-P` for all exposed ports on random host ports).

interactions.title: Does the data survive? Volume persistence simulator
interactions.description: Choose how PostgreSQL stores its data, insert rows, then recreate, down, down -v or delete the storage and see what the next container finds.

questions.prompt: Which command removes the containers and the network but keeps the PostgreSQL data?
questions.explanation: `down` keeps named volumes; `down -v` deletes the named volumes declared in the file.

questions.prompt: The app service has `SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/taskdb` and PostgreSQL is the `db` service. What happens?
options: The app's start-up fails with connection refused: localhost is the app container
questions.explanation: Inside a container `localhost` is that container. Use the service name: `jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/taskdb`.

questions.prompt: What does short-form `depends_on: [db]` guarantee?
options: PostgreSQL accepts connections before the app starts
The db container is started before the app container
The app restarts when db restarts
questions.explanation: Only start order. To wait for readiness, use `condition: service_healthy` with a database health check.

questions.prompt: You change only `app.environment` and run `docker compose up -d`. What happens?
options: Only the app container is recreated; db keeps running
questions.explanation: `up -d` compares desired and actual state and recreates only services whose configuration or image changed.

questions.prompt: A service should come back after crashes and reboots but stay stopped after an operator stops it. Which policy?
questions.explanation: `unless-stopped` restarts after crashes and daemon restarts, except for containers you stopped yourself. `on-failure` does not restart after a daemon restart.

topics.after: Why Secrets Must Never Be Committed

questions.prompt: A database password was pushed to a public repository and removed in the next commit. What is the first thing to do?
questions.explanation: The secret is still in the history, in clones and possibly in scanners' databases. Rotation is the only real fix; history rewriting comes later, if at all.

questions.prompt: `application-prod.yml` sets `server.port: 8081` and the container has `SERVER_PORT=8082`. With the prod profile active, which port is used?
questions.explanation: OS environment variables rank above every application*.yml file.

questions.prompt: Which line is safe to commit?
questions.explanation: Only the bare placeholder keeps the value out of the repository. A default inside `${…}` commits the secret too.

questions.prompt: What does Compose do with a `.env` file next to `compose.yaml`?
options: Uses it to fill `${VAR}` placeholders in compose.yaml
questions.explanation: `.env` drives interpolation in the Compose file; `env_file:` is what loads a file's lines as container variables.

interactions.title: Follow a request through Nginx
interactions.description: Choose a scenario and follow the request hop by hop: DNS, Nginx, TLS, proxy_pass, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL — and see which status the client gets.

interactions.title: Check yourself: what does Nginx's status mean?

questions.prompt: error.log: `connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream`. What did the client get?
questions.explanation: Nginx could not connect to the upstream — 502 Bad Gateway. Check whether the app runs and whether `proxy_pass` matches its port.

questions.prompt: error.log: `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream`. Status?
questions.explanation: The app accepted the connection but did not answer within `proxy_read_timeout`: 504 Gateway Timeout.

questions.prompt: A 5 MB upload fails at Nginx with 413. Which directive fixes it?
questions.explanation: Nginx's default body limit is 1 MB; raise `client_max_body_size`.

questions.prompt: Nginx runs in a container next to the `app` service. Which `proxy_pass` works?
questions.explanation: Inside the Nginx container, localhost is Nginx itself. Use the service name and the container port.

questions.prompt: Which record points `api.example.com` at the VPS's IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address (AAAA for IPv6).

questions.prompt: Certbot's HTTP-01 challenge needs which two things to be ready?
options: DNS pointing to the server and port 80 reachable
questions.explanation: Let's Encrypt fetches a token over HTTP on port 80 from the host the domain resolves to.

questions.prompt: You changed an A record with TTL 3600 ten minutes ago; some users still reach the old IP. Why?
options: Resolvers may cache the old answer for up to an hour
questions.explanation: "Propagation" is cached answers expiring; the TTL bounds it.

questions.prompt: How do you check that automatic renewal will work without issuing a real certificate?
questions.explanation: `--dry-run` runs renewal against Let's Encrypt's staging environment.

interactions.title: CI/CD pipeline simulator
interactions.description: Follow one change from git push to production in different scenarios: a clean release, a failing test, a pull request, a denied push, an automatic rollback.

questions.prompt: For a pull request, which jobs run?

code.source:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  publish:
    needs: test
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

questions.explanation: The pull_request event triggers the workflow; `publish`'s condition requires a push to main, so it is skipped.

questions.prompt: The first step of a job is `run: ./mvnw -B verify` and it fails with "No such file or directory". Why?
options: The repository was never checked out — add `actions/checkout` first
questions.explanation: Every job starts on an empty runner.

questions.prompt: `./mvnw: Permission denied` on the Linux runner, but it works on a Windows laptop. Fix?
questions.explanation: The executable bit was lost when committing from Windows; Git can record it explicitly.

questions.prompt: What does `cache: maven` on `actions/setup-java` do?
options: Caches the built JAR between jobs
Restores `~/.m2/repository` from earlier runs, keyed on the pom.xml files
questions.explanation: Dependencies are downloaded once and reused until the pom changes.

questions.prompt: Which tag should production's `.env` reference?
options: The commit SHA tag built by CI
None — use the digest of `latest` at deploy time
questions.explanation: A SHA tag is unique and traceable to tested code, and makes rollback a one-line change.

questions.prompt: Pushing to `ghcr.io` from Actions fails with `denied`. What is usually missing?
questions.explanation: `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push packages only when the job grants that permission.

questions.prompt: What is a tag, technically?
options: A movable label pointing to an image digest
questions.explanation: The digest (`sha256:…`) is immutable; tags can be moved by pushing again.
